Above ×12 there is no sound either way.

## Speed ramps

A speed ramp changes a clip's rate over time. For example, it can play at ×1,
speed up to ×4 over half a second, hold there, and slow back down.

A ramp is made of **Speed actions**. These are ordinary actions on the clip's
action lane whose end sets a rate. (For actions in general, see
[Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md).) Each Speed action:

- starts from the rate the clip is playing at when the action begins (the
  clip's own rate, or the rate an earlier Speed action ended on)
- moves to its own end rate along its curve
- keeps that end rate after it finishes, until the next Speed action

A ramped clip **keeps its place and its length** on the timeline. Speeding
part of it up makes it play further into its file, and slowing it down makes
it play less of the file. Its start, its end and every clip around it stay
where they are.

On the timeline, a Speed action's band is labelled `speed` when the track is
tall enough to show labels. When the clip's rate changes, a white line across
its action lane draws the rate over the clip's length: higher where it plays
faster, lower where it plays slower, scaled from the clip's own slowest rate
to its fastest (so a gentle ramp draws as tall as a steep one; the Speed
section has the figures). The line shows at the Medium and Large track
heights and in the Clip tab's lane, and while it is drawn a selected Speed
band leaves out its curve. A clip whose rate never changes draws no line.
The clip's filmstrip and waveform follow the ramp.

### Make a ramp in one step: Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…
  right-click **Remove from action** take the rate out of the action.
- **Keep pitch** still sets the clip's own setting, at the clip's own rate.
- **Fit to** is the clip's alone and cannot be set inside an action. Its row
  is marked ⊘.

### Changing the speed of a ramped clip

**Clip ▸ Speed…**, the Speed section's Rate with no action selected, Fit to
and the ⌥ rate stretch all scale a ramped clip's **whole** ramp by one
factor: the clip's own rate, every end rate and the length of every Speed
action. The ramp keeps its shape. For Speed…, Rate and Fit to, if scaling
would push any rate in the ramp past ×0.1 or ×1000, the scaling stops at that
limit, so the clip's rate can end up short of the rate you asked for. A ⌥
rate stretch that would do so does nothing.

Trims, slips, rolls, splits, freeze frames and transitions also follow the
ramp, so each cut or held frame is the frame the ramp actually plays at that
moment. **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** never copies a speed or a ramp.
**Detach Audio** gives the separate audio clip the same ramp.

- **Splitting inside a Speed action** keeps the picture continuous at the
  cut, with no repeated or skipped frame. With an Ease Out or Ease In Out
  curve the rate can jump at the cut. With an Ease In or Ease In Out curve
  the second half can end on a different source frame.
- **An action past the clip's end.** After a trim, or after the ramp is
  scaled, a Speed action can lie partly or wholly past the clip's end. You
  can still re-curve it, move it earlier or shorten it; only a change that
  takes it further past the end is refused. Its end rate still counts for
  the ×12 rule, even though that part never plays.
- **Transcripts and captions.** Transcribing a ramped clip places each word
  where the ramp plays it. Captions and word captions already on the timeline
  follow a later change to the ramp, as below.

### Captions follow a speed change

When you change the speed of a clip with sound, or add, move, resize, edit or
remove a Speed action on it, the captions over that clip move with its speech
in the same undo step. The step is named after the edit with "and Re-time
Captions" added, such as **Set Speed and Re-time Captions**; one undo puts the
captions back too. A drag moves them when you let go of the mouse.

- **Which captions.** Text clips on a track named "Captions" or "Captions N"
  that holds only text clips and is not locked, each lying wholly inside the
  clip you edited. A caption that runs past either edge of the clip, and
  anything on another track, is left where it is.
- **Speech the clip no longer plays.** A caption whose speech the clip no
  longer reaches is removed. A word caption page that is only partly reached
  keeps the words that still play, and its text is cut to match.
- **Newly revealed speech.** When a speed-up or a ramp makes the clip play
  further into its file, the new part gets no captions. Generate Captions
  again to caption it ([Captions](captions.md)).
- **Neighbours.** A moved caption is cut back where it would run into a
  caption that did not move. One that would start inside such a caption, or
  would end up shorter than a frame, is removed.

### When a ramp is refused

A ramp may never play past the end of the clip's media file. An edit that
would do so is refused, and the reason names what would fit:

- setting an end rate too high names **the largest end rate that fits**, or,
  if no rate down to ×0.1 fits, the latest clip end that would fit at ×0.1
- moving, resizing or removing a Speed action, or clearing its rate, names
  **the latest clip end that fits**
- a Speed Ramp… preset names **the largest rate that fits**

Speed Ramp… is also refused when:

- the span runs past the clip's end
- the span overlaps an action already on the clip, including one inside a
  Dip's or Burst's hold
- a Dip or Burst span is shorter than two frames
- the rate is on the wrong side of the starting rate (for example, a Ramp Up
  to a rate that is not faster)

A refusal changes nothing. The inspector shows the reason at its foot, and
the Speed Ramp… sheet shows it in its readout.

### Rendered audio

Two kinds of clip have their sound rendered into a separate file in the
background, saved in the project package: a clip with a speed ramp, and a
clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off. Renders run one
at a time, and a new one starts after each edit that changes the clip's
timing: a ramp, its rate, a trim or a split. Each render covers the whole
clip's sound. Undo and redo render again too, because the file from before
the edit is not kept, so the clip is briefly silent after an undo as well.
How long the silence lasts grows with the clip's length and rate: well under
a second for a 10 s clip, and a few seconds for a minute of ×4.

- **Keep pitch off:** the sound glides smoothly up and down in pitch with the
  rate, like tape, and stays in step with the picture. At a constant speed it
  plays at that speed's tape pitch, sample-exact.
- **Keep pitch on:** the sound keeps its own pitch as the speed changes.
  After a steep slow-down (for example ×2 → ×0.5) it can run up to about
  22 ms behind the picture.

While a clip's sound is still rendering, that clip plays silent in the
preview. An export waits for every render it needs (its progress reads
"Preparing…" during the wait) and never writes that sound silent. If a render
fails, the export fails with "Clip N's retimed audio could not be
rendered: …". A failed render is not tried again while Frame Job stays open:
the clip stays silent and exports that need it keep failing until you change
the clip's timing (which starts a new render) or quit and reopen Frame Job.

## Retime a range

**Clip ▸ Retime Range…** (right after Close Gap) plays the In–Out range faster
or slower on **every unlocked track** at once, and moves everything after Out
up or back so it stays in step. Use it to speed up a slow stretch of a screen
recording with its microphone and camera together. It is one undo step,
**Retime Range**.

The item needs an In–Out range and works inside a nest too, where it retimes
the nest's own tracks. The sheet has:

- **Rate**, starting at ×2, with the Speed sheet's quick picks. ×2 makes the
  range half as long, ×0.5 twice as long.
- **Preserve pitch**, which starts as the first video or audio clip in the
  range has it (on when there is none), and is set on every such clip.

**Apply** at ×1 just closes the sheet. Otherwise:

- A clip that crosses In or Out is cut there first, as Split cuts it.
- Each video or audio clip inside plays at its own rate times the Rate, so a
  ×2 clip retimed by ×2 plays at ×4. A speed ramp keeps its shape and every
  rate in it scales.
- Titles, shapes, stills, images, graphics and adjustment clips inside are
  stretched or squeezed by the same amount. A graphic keeps its own length.
- Actions keep their place in each clip.
- Markers inside the range move with the picture, and markers after it move
  with everything else. A detached sound linked to a moved clip moves with it.

Nothing changes, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector, when:

- the Rate is outside ×0.1–×1000, or the range is under two frames;
- a **locked** track has a clip after In (it would fall out of step);
- the range holds a nest clip, a caption page with timed words, or half of a
  detached pair (Attach Audio first);
- a transition touches the range;
- two markers would land on the same time;
- a clip would play faster than ×1000 or slower than ×0.1 (the message names
  the clip and the rate), or would be squeezed under one frame.

Taking a clip with sound past ×12 asks first, as below.

*Agents:* `retime_range {from, to, rate, keep_pitch?}` is the same edit. Its
answer lists the cut pieces in `new_clips` and carries `audio_left_out` and
`audio_note` when a clip crosses ×12.

## The ×12 question

A clip's sound is left out of the mix whenever it plays faster than ×12. For a
ramped clip, Frame Job looks at the **fastest rate the clip uses anywhere**:
if any rate in the ramp is above ×12, the whole clip is silent, not just the
fast part.

Before an edit takes a clip that has sound from ×12 or below to above ×12, an
alert asks first. For example: “Interview” will be silent at ×16. Frame Job
leaves a clip's audio out above ×12. The picture still plays.

When several clips would cross ×12, the alert counts them: “3 clips will be
silent at ×16.” (or “…at their new speeds.” when their rates differ), followed
by “Frame Job leaves a clip's audio out above ×12. The pictures still play.”

- **Set Speed** applies the edit as asked.
- **Cancel** changes nothing and adds no undo step. The Speed sheet and the
  Speed Ramp… sheet stay open.

The question comes from the Speed sheet, the Speed Ramp… sheet, the Retime
Range sheet and the Speed Up Typing sheet (both stay open on Cancel too), the Speed
section (Rate, its quick picks, Keep pitch, Reset and Fit to) and the ⌥ rate
stretch. A stretch is put back while the question is up, and Set Speed applies
it again. A clip that was already above ×12, or whose sound is switched off,
is not asked about.

*Agents:* no question is asked. The answer to any edit that takes a clip past
×12 carries `audio_left_out` (the clip ids) and `audio_note` (a sentence
saying the clip is now silent in the preview and the export), `retime_range`
included. `set_speed`,
`rate_stretch`, `add_speed_ramp`, `set_action`, `set_action_end` with a
`speed` and `remove_action` re-time captions as above, and their answer
carries `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed` (caption clip ids), each
only when it is not empty.

    /// Clamped to the source bound — `to ≥ start - in/speed` snapped UP to
    /// a frame, `source_window.rs`'s `earliest_start_on_grid` (spec §11,
    /// D4-5) — and to leaving at least one frame of clip. Actions are
    /// deliberately left alone: clip-relative, rebasing would drop or bake
    /// whatever fell off the front, which is lossy and makes trimming back
    /// out not an identity. On a RAMPED clip the actions keep their clip
    /// time too, so `in` advances by round(S(Δ)) moving in and at the base
    /// rate moving out, and the edge is held where the clip still fits its
    /// media (`front_edge_held`, spec §11 SR-18 (c)): what plays after the
    /// new start can change. `text.words` are the opposite, on purpose
    /// (spec §11, W-3): a word is anchored to speech that stays where it is
    /// on the timeline, so every word is rebased by the trim's delta and a
    /// word trimmed off the front keeps its (negative) time. A graphic's
    /// `in` advances by the same delta (road map 10's G-9), with no speed
    /// and no head bound, never below 0.
    ///
    /// Without `alone`, a linked partner whose start is this clip's is
    /// trimmed to the same `to` after it, by its own clamps; with it, the
    /// clip moves alone — the J-cut (spec §11 AU-93, `carried_edge`).
    pub fn trim_start(&self, clip: u32, to: Ticks, alone: bool) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
        self.carried_edge(
            clip,
            alone,
            |target, partner| partner.start == target.start,
            |project, id| project.trim_start_one(id, to),
        )
    }

    fn trim_start_one(&self, clip: u32, to: Ticks) -> Result<Outcome, String> {

---
title: Edit a ramped clip
description: What a speed change, trim, split or freeze frame does to a clip with a speed ramp, and why Frame Job sometimes won't make the edit.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Once a clip has a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), your ordinary edits still work on it. This page says what each one does to the ramp, and what stops an edit that would break it.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Speed…"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section', '⌥-drag a clip\'s end edge', 'The action lane']}
  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'set_action']}
/>

## Scale a whole ramp

These all change a ramped clip's speed by scaling the whole ramp by one factor:

- **Clip ▸ Speed…**
- **Rate** in the [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/), with no action selected
- **Fit to** in the Speed section
- The ⌥ [rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) on the clip's end edge

The clip's own rate, every end rate and the length of every Speed action scale together, so the ramp keeps its shape and the clip still plays the same stretch of its file. The clip itself gets shorter or longer. A ramp from ×1 to ×2 scaled by ×2 becomes a ramp from ×2 to ×4, in half the time. With a ramped clip selected, the Speed sheet's readout ends "Each speed ramp keeps its shape: the rates it names scale with the base rate."

No rate in a clip can go below ×0.1 or above ×1000, and what happens at those limits depends on how you made the change:

| You used | At a limit |
| --- | --- |
| **Speed…**, **Rate** or **Fit to** | Scaling stops at the limit, so the clip's rate can end up short of the rate you asked for. |
| The ⌥ rate stretch | Nothing happens. |
| [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) | It scales a ramp the same way, but Frame Job won't make the edit, and the reason names the clip and the rate. |

To change one rate inside the ramp instead, select its action. **Rate** then sets that action's end rate. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/).

## Edits follow the ramp

Trims, slips, rolls, splits, freeze frames and transitions all read the ramp, so each cut or held frame is the frame the ramp actually plays at that moment.

| Edit | What it does on a ramped clip |
| --- | --- |
| Trim the start | The frame under the edge stays put. The Speed actions stay the same distance from the clip's start, so what plays after the new start can change. The edge stops where the clip would otherwise play past the end of its file. |
| Trim the end | The Speed actions don't move. How far you can pull the end out depends on the rate the clip reaches, not on its own rate. |
| Roll | The later clip's start behaves as a start trim, and the earlier clip's end as an end trim. |
| Slip | The source moves at the clip's own rate, and the Speed actions stay where they are. It stops so the clip never plays past the end of its file. |
| [Split](#split-inside-a-speed-action) | The two halves meet at the frame the ramp plays at the cut, and the second half starts at the rate playing there. |
| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) | The still holds the frame the ramp plays at that moment. |
| [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | The separate audio clip gets the same ramp. |

**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** never copies a speed or a ramp, in either direction.

Transcribing a ramped clip places each word where the ramp plays it. Captions already on the timeline [follow a later change to the ramp](/speed/captions-and-speed/).

## Split inside a Speed action

Splitting partway through a Speed action keeps the picture continuous at the cut, with no repeated or skipped frame. The action becomes two, one on each half. The first ends at whatever rate makes the picture meet at the cut, and the second keeps the original end rate.

The action's curve matters here:

- With **Ease Out** or **Ease In Out**, the rate can jump at the cut.
- With **Ease In** or **Ease In Out**, the second half can end on a different frame of the file than the unsplit clip did. If it would then play past the end of the file, its end rate is lowered to the largest that fits.

## Filmstrip and waveform

A ramped clip's filmstrip and waveform follow the ramp, so what you see at a point on the timeline is what plays there. A stretch at a high rate shows more of the file in the same space.

## An action past the clip's end

After a trim, or after a ramp is scaled, a Speed action can lie partly or wholly past the clip's end. It stays on the clip, and you can still change its curve, move it earlier or shorten it. Frame Job only stops a change that takes it further past the end.

Its end rate still counts for the [×12 rule](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/), even though that part never plays. If a clip has gone silent because of a rate you can't hear or see playing, look for an action like this.

## When a ramp is refused

A ramped clip keeps its place and its length on the timeline, so a ramp can't play past the end of the clip's file. Frame Job won't make an edit that would, and the reason says what would fit:

| You tried to | The reason names |
| --- | --- |
| Set an end rate too high | The largest end rate that fits. If no rate down to ×0.1 fits, the latest clip end that would fit at ×0.1. |
| Move, resize or remove a Speed action, or clear its rate | The latest clip end that fits. |
| Apply a **Speed Ramp…** preset | The largest rate that fits, or says that no rate does. |

**Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** also won't apply a preset when:

- the span runs past the clip's end
- the span overlaps an action already on the clip, including one inside a Dip's or Burst's hold
- a Dip or Burst span is shorter than two frames
- the rate is on the wrong side of the starting rate, such as a Ramp Up to a rate that isn't faster

A clip with [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) is linked to its audio, and no speed or ramp edit will change it. The reason says to use Attach Audio first.

When an edit is refused, nothing changes. Frame Job beeps, makes no undo step, and shows the reason:

- **At the foot of the inspector**, after the word "Refused:". It stays until the project changes or you click it.
- **In the Speed Ramp sheet's readout**, as you adjust the sheet. **Apply** is dimmed until the preset fits.

A reason gives times in ticks, and there are 600,000 ticks in a second.

## Related

- [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/)
- [Make a speed ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/)
- [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/)
- [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/)
- [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/)

---
title: Sound on a ramp
description: How Frame Job renders the sound of a ramped clip in the background, why the clip goes silent for a moment, and what an export does about it.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A clip whose speed changes as it plays can't play its sound straight from the file, so Frame Job renders that sound in the background. While it renders, the clip is silent in the preview. An export always waits for it.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section ▸ Keep pitch"
  tools={['set_speed', 'export']}
/>

## Rendered audio

Two kinds of clip have their sound rendered into a separate file:

- a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), with **Keep pitch** on or off
- a clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with **Keep pitch** off

A clip at a constant speed with **Keep pitch** on isn't rendered, and neither is a clip above ×12, because [it has no sound](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).

There's nothing to start. A new render begins after each edit that changes the clip's timing, such as a ramp, its rate, a trim or a split, and after you change **Keep pitch**. During a drag, it waits until you let go.

Each render covers the whole clip's sound, so how long it takes grows with the clip's length and rate. Renders run one at a time, in the background, so you can keep editing. An edit that makes a render out of date drops it, so a run of quick edits doesn't queue up work.

The files are saved inside the project package, in `cache/ramp-audio/`, and Frame Job can rebuild them. Until a new project is saved, they're in a temporary folder. [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) doesn't copy them, so the new project renders its own.

## Keep pitch off

The sound glides smoothly up and down in pitch with the rate, like tape, and stays in step with the picture. At a constant speed it plays at that speed's tape pitch, exact to the sample.

## Keep pitch on

The sound keeps its own pitch as the speed changes. After a steep slow-down, for example ×2 to ×0.5, it can run up to about 22 ms behind the picture.

See [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) for the control itself.

## Silent while it renders

While a clip's sound is rendering, that clip plays silent in the preview. Everything else on the timeline plays as usual, and the clip's sound comes back on its own when the render finishes.

## Undo and redo render again

Undo and redo start a render too, because the file from before the edit isn't kept. The clip is briefly silent then as well.

## Exports wait for it

An export waits for every render it needs and never writes that sound silent. Its progress reads **Preparing…** during the wait, and you can cancel it there. This covers speed ramps and clips at a constant speed other than ×1 with **Keep pitch** off.

An image sequence has no sound, so it doesn't wait.

## A failed render

If a render fails, an export that needs it stops with this message, naming the clip:

> Clip N's retimed audio could not be rendered: …

Frame Job doesn't try a failed render again while it stays open. The clip stays silent, and exports that need it keep failing, until you change the clip's timing, which starts a new render, or quit and reopen Frame Job.

## Related

- [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/)
- [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/)
- [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)

The files are saved inside the project package, in `cache/ramp-audio/`, and Frame Job can rebuild them. Until a new project is saved, they're in a temporary folder. [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) doesn't copy them, so the new project renders its own.

## Keep pitch off

The sound glides smoothly up and down in pitch with the rate, like tape, and stays in step with the picture. At a constant speed it plays at that speed's tape pitch, exact to the sample.

## Keep pitch on

The sound keeps its own pitch as the speed changes. After a steep slow-down, for example ×2 to ×0.5, it can run up to about 22 ms behind the picture.

See [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) for the control itself.

## Silent while it renders

While a clip's sound is rendering, that clip plays silent in the preview. Everything else on the timeline plays as usual, and the clip's sound comes back on its own when the render finishes.

## Undo and redo render again

Undo and redo start a render too, because the file from before the edit isn't kept. The clip is briefly silent then as well.

## Exports wait for it

An export waits for every render it needs and never writes that sound silent. Its progress reads **Preparing…** during the wait, and you can cancel it there. This covers speed ramps and clips at a constant speed other than ×1 with **Keep pitch** off.

An image sequence has no sound, so it doesn't wait.

## A failed render

If a render fails, an export that needs it stops with this message, naming the clip:

> Clip N's retimed audio could not be rendered: …

Frame Job doesn't try a failed render again while it stays open. The clip stays silent, and exports that need it keep failing, until you change the clip's timing, which starts a new render, or quit and reopen Frame Job.

- [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)

---
title: Captions follow a speed change
description: How captions stay on the speech when a clip's speed or ramp changes, which ones move, and which ones Frame Job removes.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When you change the speed of a clip with sound, the captions over it move with its speech, so they stay on the words you hear. There's nothing to turn on.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…']}
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section', 'The action lane', '⌥-drag a clip\'s end edge']}
  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'add_speed_ramp', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
/>

## What moves them

Captions move when you:

- change the clip's speed, with **Clip ▸ Speed…**, the Speed section or the ⌥ rate stretch
- add a ramp with **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…**
- add, move, resize, edit or remove a Speed action on the clip

The captions move in the same undo step as the edit, so one undo puts them back too. The step is named after the edit with "and Re-time Captions" added, such as **Set Speed and Re-time Captions**. A drag moves them when you let go of the mouse.

The clip has to be one captions could have been made from: it plays media with sound, its audio is on, and it isn't reversed.

## Which captions move

A caption moves when all of these are true:

- It's a text clip on a track named **Captions** or **Captions N**, such as **Captions 2**.
- That track holds only text clips and isn't locked.
- It lies wholly inside the clip you edited.

A caption that runs past either edge of the clip stays where it is, and so does anything on another track.

## Speech the clip no longer plays

Slowing a clip down can stop it reaching the end of the speech it played before.

A caption whose speech the clip no longer reaches is removed. A word caption page that's only partly reached keeps the words that still play, and its text is cut to match.

## Newly revealed speech

When a speed-up or a ramp makes the clip play further into its file, the new part gets no captions. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) again to caption it.

## Neighbouring captions

A moved caption is cut back where it would run into a caption that didn't move. One that would start inside such a caption, or end up shorter than a frame, is removed.

## Good to know

- Only speed and ramp edits move captions. A trim, slip or split leaves them where they are.
- [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) works differently. It stretches or squeezes a text clip in the range along with everything else, and it won't run over a caption page with timed words.
- Frame Job checks every new place before it commits. If they don't all work out, the speed edit goes through on its own and the captions stay where they were.

## Related

- [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/)
- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)
- [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/)
- [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/)

---
title: Retime Range
description: Play the stretch between In and Out faster or slower on every unlocked track at once, and keep everything after it in step.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Retime Range plays the stretch between In and Out faster or slower on every unlocked track at once, and moves everything after Out up or back to stay in step. Use it to speed up a slow part of a screen recording with its microphone and camera together.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Retime Range…"
  tools="retime_range"
  needs="An in/out range."
/>

## Retime a range

<Steps>

1. Set [In and Out](/timeline/in-out-range/) around the stretch. The menu item is dimmed without them, and while another sheet is open.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Retime Range…**. It has no keyboard shortcut.

3. Set the **Rate**, and tick or untick **Preserve pitch**.

4. Choose **Apply**.

</Steps>

The whole edit is one undo step, **Retime Range**.

## The sheet

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Rate:** | How much faster the range plays. ×2 makes it half as long, and ×0.5 twice as long. The **Presets** pull-down offers 0.25×, 0.50×, 1×, 1.5×, 2×, 4×, 10× and 100×. | ×2 | ×0.1 to ×1000 |
| **Preserve pitch** | Sets the pitch setting on every video or audio clip in the range, as [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) does on one clip. | As the first video or audio clip on an unlocked track in the range has it, or on when there is none | |

**Apply** at ×1 closes the sheet and changes nothing. At any other rate it retimes the range.

If the rate takes a clip with sound past ×12, Frame Job [asks first](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/), because above ×12 a clip's audio is left out. **Set Speed** closes the sheet and applies the edit. **Cancel** leaves the sheet open with nothing changed.

## What happens in the range

### Clips across an edge

A clip that crosses In or Out is cut there first, as [Split](/editing/split/) cuts it. Only the piece inside the range changes speed.

### Rates multiply

Each video or audio clip inside plays at its own rate times the **Rate**, so a ×2 clip retimed by ×2 plays at ×4. A [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/#scale-a-whole-ramp) keeps its shape, and every rate in it scales.

### Titles, shapes and stills

Titles, shapes, stills, images, graphics and adjustment clips inside are stretched or squeezed by the same amount. A graphic with a length of its own keeps it.

### Actions

Actions keep their place in each clip, at the same fraction of its length. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).

### Markers and detached sound

Markers inside the range move with the picture, and markers after it move with everything else. A detached sound linked to a moved clip moves with it.

## Inside a nest

Retime Range works inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), where it retimes the nest's own tracks and uses the nest's own In and Out. A nest has no markers of its own, so none moves.

## When a range can't be retimed

Nothing changes, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. Frame Job checks these in order and stops at the first one it meets:

| What stops it | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The rate is outside ×0.1 to ×1000. | The sheet's field keeps you inside this range, so this one comes up with an agent. |
| The range is under two frames. | Widen the range. |
| A locked track has a clip that ends after In. It would fall out of step. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/), or move the clip. |
| The range touches a nest clip. | Move the range off it, or retime inside the nest. |
| The range touches a caption page with timed words. | Move the range off it. |
| The range touches half of a detached pair. | Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
| A transition touches the range. | Move the range off it, or remove the transition. |
| Two markers would land on the same time. | Move one of them first. |
| A clip would play faster than ×1000 or slower than ×0.1. The message names the clip and the rate. | Pick a gentler rate, or set the clip's own speed first. |
| A clip would be squeezed under one frame. The message names it. | Pick a gentler rate. |

A clip only has to overlap the range to count, so a nest or a detached clip that crosses In or Out stops the edit too.

## With an agent

`retime_range` makes the same edit, but it takes the range as times, so it needs no In and Out. It never asks about ×12: the clip's audio is left out, and the answer says so. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).

## Related

- [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/)
- [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/)
- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
- [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/)

---
title: Edit a ramped clip
description: What a speed change, trim, split or freeze frame does to a clip with a speed ramp, and why Frame Job sometimes won't make the edit.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Once a clip has a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), your ordinary edits still work on it. This page says what each one does to the ramp, and what stops an edit that would break it.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Speed…"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section', '⌥-drag a clip\'s end edge', 'The action lane']}
  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'set_action']}
/>

## Scale a whole ramp

These all change a ramped clip's speed by scaling the whole ramp by one factor:

- **Clip ▸ Speed…**
- **Rate** in the [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/), with no action selected
- **Fit to** in the Speed section
- The ⌥ [rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) on the clip's end edge

The clip's own rate, every end rate and the length of every Speed action scale together, so the ramp keeps its shape and the clip still plays the same stretch of its file. The clip itself gets shorter or longer. A ramp from ×1 to ×2 scaled by ×2 becomes a ramp from ×2 to ×4, in half the time. With a ramped clip selected, the Speed sheet's readout ends "Each speed ramp keeps its shape: the rates it names scale with the base rate."

No rate in a clip can go below ×0.1 or above ×1000, and what happens at those limits depends on how you made the change:

| You used | At a limit |
| --- | --- |
| **Speed…**, **Rate** or **Fit to** | Scaling stops at the limit, so the clip's rate can end up short of the rate you asked for. |
| The ⌥ rate stretch | Nothing happens. |
| [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) | It scales a ramp the same way, but Frame Job won't make the edit, and the reason names the clip and the rate. |

To change one rate inside the ramp instead, select its action. **Rate** then sets that action's end rate. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/).

## Edits follow the ramp

Trims, slips, rolls, splits, freeze frames and transitions all read the ramp, so each cut or held frame is the frame the ramp actually plays at that moment.

| Edit | What it does on a ramped clip |
| --- | --- |
| Trim the start | The frame under the edge stays put. The Speed actions stay the same distance from the clip's start, so what plays after the new start can change. The edge stops where the clip would otherwise play past the end of its file. |
| Trim the end | The Speed actions don't move. How far you can pull the end out depends on the rate the clip reaches, not on its own rate. |
| Roll | The later clip's start behaves as a start trim, and the earlier clip's end as an end trim. |
| Slip | The source moves at the clip's own rate, and the Speed actions stay where they are. It stops so the clip never plays past the end of its file. |
| [Split](#split-inside-a-speed-action) | The two halves meet at the frame the ramp plays at the cut, and the second half starts at the rate playing there. |
| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) | The still holds the frame the ramp plays at that moment. |
| [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | The separate audio clip gets the same ramp. |

**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** never copies a speed or a ramp, in either direction.

Transcribing a ramped clip places each word where the ramp plays it. Captions already on the timeline [follow a later change to the ramp](/speed/captions-and-speed/).

## Split inside a Speed action

Splitting partway through a Speed action keeps the picture continuous at the cut, with no repeated or skipped frame. The action becomes two, one on each half. The first ends at whatever rate makes the picture meet at the cut, and the second keeps the original end rate.

The action's curve matters here:

- With **Ease Out** or **Ease In Out**, the rate can jump at the cut.
- With **Ease In** or **Ease In Out**, the second half can end on a different frame of the file than the unsplit clip did. If it would then play past the end of the file, its end rate is lowered to the largest that fits.

## Filmstrip and waveform

A ramped clip's filmstrip and waveform follow the ramp, so what you see at a point on the timeline is what plays there. A stretch at a high rate shows more of the file in the same space.

## An action past the clip's end

After a trim, or after a ramp is scaled, a Speed action can lie partly or wholly past the clip's end. It stays on the clip, and you can still change its curve, move it earlier or shorten it. Frame Job only stops a change that takes it further past the end.

Its end rate still counts for the [×12 rule](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/), even though that part never plays. If a clip has gone silent because of a rate you can't hear or see playing, look for an action like this.

## When a ramp is refused

A ramped clip keeps its place and its length on the timeline, so a ramp can't play past the end of the clip's file. Frame Job won't make an edit that would, and the reason says what would fit:

| You tried to | The reason names |
| --- | --- |
| Set an end rate too high | The largest end rate that fits. If no rate down to ×0.1 fits, the latest clip end that would fit at ×0.1. |
| Move, resize or remove a Speed action, or clear its rate | The latest clip end that fits. |
| Apply a **Speed Ramp…** preset | The largest rate that fits, or says that no rate does. |

**Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** also won't apply a preset when:

- the span runs past the clip's end
- the span overlaps an action already on the clip, including one inside a Dip's or Burst's hold
- a Dip or Burst span is shorter than two frames
- the rate is on the wrong side of the starting rate, such as a Ramp Up to a rate that isn't faster

A clip with [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) is linked to its audio, and no speed or ramp edit will change it. The reason says to use Attach Audio first.

When an edit is refused, nothing changes. Frame Job beeps, makes no undo step, and shows the reason:

- **At the foot of the inspector**, after the word "Refused:". It stays until the project changes or you click it.
- **In the Speed Ramp sheet's readout**, as you adjust the sheet. **Apply** is dimmed until the preset fits.

A reason gives times in ticks, and there are 600,000 ticks in a second.

## Related

- [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/)
- [Make a speed ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/)
- [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/)
- [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/)
- [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/)

## Related

- [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/)
- [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/)
- [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)

---
title: Captions follow a speed change
description: How captions stay on the speech when a clip's speed or ramp changes, which ones move, and which ones Frame Job removes.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When you change the speed of a clip with sound, the captions over it move with its speech, so they stay on the words you hear. There's nothing to turn on.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…']}
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section', 'The action lane', '⌥-drag a clip\'s end edge']}
  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'add_speed_ramp', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
/>

## What moves them

Captions move when you:

- change the clip's speed, with **Clip ▸ Speed…**, the Speed section or the ⌥ rate stretch
- add a ramp with **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…**
- add, move, resize, edit or remove a Speed action on the clip

The captions move in the same undo step as the edit, so one undo puts them back too. The step is named after the edit with "and Re-time Captions" added, such as **Set Speed and Re-time Captions**. A drag moves them when you let go of the mouse.

The clip has to be one captions could have been made from: it plays media with sound, its audio is on, and it isn't reversed.

## Which captions move

A caption moves when all of these are true:

- It's a text clip on a track named **Captions** or **Captions N**, such as **Captions 2**.
- That track holds only text clips and isn't locked.
- It lies wholly inside the clip you edited.

A caption that runs past either edge of the clip stays where it is, and so does anything on another track.

## Speech the clip no longer plays

Slowing a clip down can stop it reaching the end of the speech it played before.

A caption whose speech the clip no longer reaches is removed. A word caption page that's only partly reached keeps the words that still play, and its text is cut to match.

## Newly revealed speech

When a speed-up or a ramp makes the clip play further into its file, the new part gets no captions. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) again to caption it.

## Neighbouring captions

A moved caption is cut back where it would run into a caption that didn't move. One that would start inside such a caption, or end up shorter than a frame, is removed.

## Good to know

- Only speed and ramp edits move captions. A trim, slip or split leaves them where they are.
- [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) works differently. It stretches or squeezes a text clip in the range along with everything else, and it won't run over a caption page with timed words.
- Frame Job checks every new place before it commits. If they don't all work out, the speed edit goes through on its own and the captions stay where they were.

## Related

- [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/)
- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)
- [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/)
- [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/)

---
title: Retime Range
description: Play the stretch between In and Out faster or slower on every unlocked track at once, and keep everything after it in step.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Retime Range plays the stretch between In and Out faster or slower on every unlocked track at once, and moves everything after Out up or back to stay in step. Use it to speed up a slow part of a screen recording with its microphone and camera together.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Retime Range…"
  tools="retime_range"
  needs="An in/out range."
/>

## Retime a range

<Steps>

1. Set [In and Out](/timeline/in-out-range/) around the stretch. The menu item is dimmed without them, and while another sheet is open.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Retime Range…**. It has no keyboard shortcut.

3. Set the **Rate**, and tick or untick **Preserve pitch**.

4. Choose **Apply**.

</Steps>

The whole edit is one undo step, **Retime Range**.

## The sheet

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Rate:** | How much faster the range plays. ×2 makes it half as long, and ×0.5 twice as long. The **Presets** pull-down offers 0.25×, 0.50×, 1×, 1.5×, 2×, 4×, 10× and 100×. | ×2 | ×0.1 to ×1000 |
| **Preserve pitch** | Sets the pitch setting on every video or audio clip in the range, as [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) does on one clip. | As the first video or audio clip on an unlocked track in the range has it, or on when there is none | |

**Apply** at ×1 closes the sheet and changes nothing. At any other rate it retimes the range.

If the rate takes a clip with sound past ×12, Frame Job [asks first](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/), because above ×12 a clip's audio is left out. **Set Speed** closes the sheet and applies the edit. **Cancel** leaves the sheet open with nothing changed.

## What happens in the range

### Clips across an edge

A clip that crosses In or Out is cut there first, as [Split](/editing/split/) cuts it. Only the piece inside the range changes speed.

### Rates multiply

Each video or audio clip inside plays at its own rate times the **Rate**, so a ×2 clip retimed by ×2 plays at ×4. A [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/#scale-a-whole-ramp) keeps its shape, and every rate in it scales.

### Titles, shapes and stills

Titles, shapes, stills, images, graphics and adjustment clips inside are stretched or squeezed by the same amount. A graphic with a length of its own keeps it.

### Actions

Actions keep their place in each clip, at the same fraction of its length. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).

### Markers and detached sound

Markers inside the range move with the picture, and markers after it move with everything else. A detached sound linked to a moved clip moves with it.

## Inside a nest

Retime Range works inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), where it retimes the nest's own tracks and uses the nest's own In and Out. A nest has no markers of its own, so none moves.

## When a range can't be retimed

Nothing changes, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. Frame Job checks these in order and stops at the first one it meets:

| What stops it | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The rate is outside ×0.1 to ×1000. | The sheet's field keeps you inside this range, so this one comes up with an agent. |
| The range is under two frames. | Widen the range. |
| A locked track has a clip that ends after In. It would fall out of step. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/), or move the clip. |
| The range touches a nest clip. | Move the range off it, or retime inside the nest. |
| The range touches a caption page with timed words. | Move the range off it. |
| The range touches half of a detached pair. | Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
| A transition touches the range. | Move the range off it, or remove the transition. |
| Two markers would land on the same time. | Move one of them first. |
| A clip would play faster than ×1000 or slower than ×0.1. The message names the clip and the rate. | Pick a gentler rate, or set the clip's own speed first. |
| A clip would be squeezed under one frame. The message names it. | Pick a gentler rate. |

A clip only has to overlap the range to count, so a nest or a detached clip that crosses In or Out stops the edit too.

## With an agent

`retime_range` makes the same edit, but it takes the range as times, so it needs no In and Out. It never asks about ×12: the clip's audio is left out, and the answer says so. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).

## Related

- [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/)
- [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/)
- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
- [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/)
